abstract: \textbf{Summary.} Six ordered categorical attributes, four imbalanced classes (smallest [[P/minority_share|pct1]]), no numeric columns, no test file. Here the comparison is decisive: HGB beats LR by [[R/comparison/bootstrap_diff_B_minus_A/f1_macro/mean|+3]] macro-F1 (95\% CI [[R/comparison/bootstrap_diff_B_minus_A/f1_macro/ci/0|+3]] to [[R/comparison/bootstrap_diff_B_minus_A/f1_macro/ci/1|+3]]), because the target is defined by interacting rules that an additive model cannot express.
issues_table: Primary metric macro-F1; \texttt{class\_weight} searched; stratified folds.
LR: one-hot without scaling; HGB: native categorical splits; no pooling needed.
data: [[P/n_train|int]] training / [[P/n_test|int]] hold-out rows, no missing values or duplicates; the profiler raised only [[P/n_flags|int]] flag. %%issues_table%%
features: Nothing to engineer: every attribute is a design input. The levels are ordered (low $<$ med $<$ high $<$ vhigh), and a numeric encoding could help a linear model; the skill keeps them nominal because the order of \texttt{doors}=`5more' and \texttt{persons}=`more' is not numeric. This choice is worth challenging, and the next ablation to add.
training: LR (multinomial, one-hot) vs.\ HGB with native categorical splits; [[L/cv/folds|int]]-fold CV because $n<2000$; macro-F1 for refit. HGB's \texttt{max\_leaf\_nodes} first landed on its upper boundary (64), so the range was widened once to 128 per the skill's rule; the re-run selected [[R/models/hgb/best_params/max_leaf_nodes|int]]. Stopping: LR converged in [[R/models/lr/fit/n_iter|int]] iterations; HGB early-stopped after [[R/models/hgb/fit/n_iter|int]] rounds. %%config_table%%
evaluation: %%results_table%% %%figure%% HGB classifies the whole hold-out correctly. LR's errors concentrate where interactions matter: [[R/models/lr/test/confusion/2/0|int]] \emph{unacc} cars predicted \emph{acc}. McNemar: [[R/comparison/mcnemar/A_wrong_B_right|int]] rows only HGB gets right, [[R/comparison/mcnemar/A_right_B_wrong|int]] the reverse ($p$ [[R/comparison/mcnemar/p_exact|p]]). Native vs.\ one-hot encoding for HGB makes no detectable difference here (Table~\ref{tab:ablation}). %%ablation_table%%
findings: Where the main report found a largely additive signal, this dataset is the opposite case, and the same two-model design exposes it: a perfect tree ensemble against a linear model at macro-F1 [[R/models/lr/test/f1_macro|3]]. The perfect hold-out score should not be over-read: the dataset is a noise-free enumeration of a known rule hierarchy.
figure_caption: Hold-out set. (a) Per-class F1. (b, c) Confusion matrices (arg-max predictions).
